subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation and SLOs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-corp.com>, Priya Patel <priya.patel@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation and SLOs

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on scope for dedicated capacity performance validation: 

Summary from today's discovery:
- Target latency (p95): 120ms for single-turn text generation (max prompt + 256 tokens).
- Throughput: baseline 200 requests/min with peaks up to 400 requests/min during promotions.
- Concurrency: expected 40 concurrent active requests during peak.
- Streaming: partial-token streaming required for UX on mobile. We confirmed you want chunked streaming with latency SLO intact.
- Model: planning to serve a 7B open model variant (quantized 4-bit) for the first phase; possible 13B in Q4.

What Redwood will validate in Dedicated trial:
1) GPU sizing comparison (A100 40GB vs T4x2 equivalent) and reserve throughput we can guarantee.
2) End-to-end latency and p95 for cold vs warm paths.
3) Streaming performance and partial-token delivery times.
4) Autoscaling behavior under synthetic load and how it affects p95.

Proposed test plan (attached): perf_test_plan.xlsx — includes test cases, traffic profiles, and acceptance criteria.

Immediate asks for you: please confirm the p95 target above (120ms) and whether you want us to include the 13B model in the initial validation. Also confirm any compliance or network constraints for the private VPC tests.

Next steps / timeline:
- You confirm targets & model scope (this week).
- Redwood shares an appointment for a 2-hour validation kickoff and hands-on run (target: next week).
- Post-validation: we'll share gpu_benchmark_results.csv and a recommendation for reserved capacity and cost estimates.

Thanks — looping in Aditya (SE) who will run the validation with me.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Patel <priya.patel@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation and SLOs

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the p95 target of 120ms is what our product team has prioritized for checkout flows. A few clarifications: 

- The 200 req/min baseline is accurate; the 400 rpm peak is during marketing spikes (we can tolerate short bursts beyond that if the average holds).
- Concurrent sessions: 40 is the conservative estimate; we can provision headroom to 60 if needed.
- Streaming: important — we need <50ms first-byte for streaming starts on mobile over 4G.

Include the 13B as a stretch goal for the validation but we don't need full production billing for it — a comparison run is fine. For private VPC tests we have a transit firewall that occasionally blocks ephemeral ports; Aditya, happy to share our network contact and firewall rules.

Also attaching the high-level workload doc we referenced.

Alex
Head of Product, Acme Retail
alex.johnson@acme-corp.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-corp.com>, Priya Patel <priya.patel@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation and SLOs

Thanks Alex — that helps. Quick responses to the items so we can lock the validation scope: 

- We'll include both 7B (primary) and 13B (stretch) runs. 13B will be run as a comparison with smaller reservation to measure delta in p95 and cost.
- Streaming first-byte target: we'll aim for <50ms on 4G as a validation threshold; note this will be sensitive to network & client side RTT — we will control for client RTT during the benchmark.
- Concurrency: we'll provision headroom to 60 concurrent for the validation so we can show both baseline and 1.5x headroom behavior.
- GPU options: initial comparison will be A100 40GB (single) vs T4x2 (two smaller cards / multi-instance). We'll measure reserved throughput expressed as RPS per GPU pool and the p95 under sustained load.

Aditya and Rishi will run the benchmark. Proposed kickoff: Wed 30 Jun 2026, 10:00–12:00 PT. Please confirm availability and provide the network contact for firewall rules.

Attaching the perf test plan and an early template for results (we'll fill gpu_benchmark_results.csv during the run).

—
Marissa

[Attachment: gpu_benchmark_results.csv (text/csv)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-corp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation and SLOs — validation plan & checklist

Alex / team — thanks for confirming. A couple of practical items before the kickoff: 

1) Network / firewall — Alex, please send the contact and a list of IP ranges we should whitelist. For VPC runs we need ephemeral port access for the control plane and the load generator.
2) Test harness — we'll use our internal load runner (continuous batching enabled) to generate both steady-state and burst profiles. Expect ~15 minutes for warm-up per config.
3) Success criteria (what we'll demonstrate during the run):
   - 7B model on A100: reserved throughput >= 100 RPS with p95 <= 120ms, streaming first-byte <= 50ms for controlled client RTT.
   - 7B model on T4x2: reserved throughput >= 60 RPS with p95 <= 200ms (comparison).
   - 13B comparison: note expected p95 increase; we'll capture token-level timing and cost per 1k tokens.
4) Deliverables within 48 hours post-run: gpu_benchmark_results.csv, config files, and a recommended reserved capacity (GPU type + count) with cost estimate.

Proposed checklist for Wed 30 Jun kickoff: 
- Acme: firewall contact + whitelist
- Acme: sample payloads and streaming client (we can provide a lightweight JS client)
- Redwood: reserved GPU pool ready, load runner, monitoring/tracing hooks enabled
- Redwood: run schedule & raw metrics sharing (in Drive link we will share during kickoff)

If those look good I'll schedule the kickoff and send calendar invites.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Staff Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
